items.title: Sid Davilla Interview, 1969-04-17
items.q: I had a talk with Ronnie Cole last week

ctx.x: changing? For instance, like these new motels, hotels they're building here, they've got three new ones in the last few years. I don't know what's going to happen to Bourbon Street, Tom, because it's been a busy street, and it's a lot busier on the outside than it is on the inside, actually, when you read the register in the morning. That's true.

But it has attracted a lot of attention and a lot of investment people. In the next block, in the next block, there are two dress shops, and there will be another restaurant going up. And there will be another restaurant going up. Instant food, fast food, and propositions. And on orange juice concern, nationally known, they've opened up down the street, and they wanted to lease this place for me to put an orange juice stand. People are selling canned beans, hot water, and bamboo bamboo bamboo bamboo bamboo bamboo…
Well, I know what you mean. I agree with you that it is definitely busier on the outside than the inside. Do you think this is a recent trend?
